lines: # Shared source assets
Use this folder for source assets that have no other owner. Unreal assets stay in the Unreal project.
A local commit is not a backup. Keep a second copy before discarding originals.
## Categories
| Folder | Contents |
| `environments/kits/` | Reusable modular pieces: walls, floors, trim. |
| `environments/locations/` | Assembled places built from kits. |
| `materials/` | Shared materials and textures. |
| `characters/` | Characters and creatures. |
| `props/` | Standalone objects. |
| `effects/` | Visual effects sources. |
| `audio/` | Sound sources. |
| `ui/` | Interface art. |
## One folder per asset
```text
assets/<category>/<asset_id>/
├── asset.json     Explicit mapping from source to Unreal (tracked)
├── source/        Editable originals: .blend, .hip, textures (tracked, Git LFS)
└── exports/       Generated FBX/GLB/USD output (ignored, rebuildable)
- `asset_id` is lowercase kebab-case, for example `stone-wall-a`, and matches the folder name.
- `source/` holds the only originals. `exports/` is disposable: never put a unique file there.
- Simulation and geometry caches (`.vdb`, `.bgeo.sc`, bakes) live outside this repository.
- Prefer `.usda` or `.usdc` over bare `.usd`, so text and binary files are told apart.
## asset.json
Every asset folder has an `asset.json` (see `templates/asset.example.json`). It states, without guessing:
- `schema_version`: currently `1`.
- `asset_id`: same as the folder name.
- `source_files`: paths inside `source/`.
- `outputs`: one entry per exported file with `source`, `export`, `unreal_package` (a folder starting with `/Game/`), `object_name`, and `import_settings`.
- `tool_versions`: the exact Blender, Houdini and Unreal versions actually used.
Paths are relative to the asset folder and use forward slashes. No absolute paths, no `..`, no symlinks out of the folder.
Asset IDs and Unreal destinations must be unique across all assets.

lines: # Blender
Project Blender scripts and add-ons live here.
Save Blender sources under `assets/<category>/<asset_id>/source/` and describe them in `asset.json`. See `assets/README.md`.
Exports go in that asset's ignored `exports/` folder. Keep bakes and caches outside the repository.
# Houdini
Project Houdini scripts and HDA tooling live here.
Save Houdini sources (`.hip`, HDAs) under `assets/<category>/<asset_id>/source/` and describe them in `asset.json`. See `assets/README.md`.
Exports go in that asset's ignored `exports/` folder. Keep geometry and simulation caches outside the repository.
Houdini output reaches Unreal as exported files unless a live bridge has been installed and verified for this project.

purpose: `{{project}}` is a game workspace: design, the Unreal project, shared source assets and the tools that move assets into the engine.
rules: - One folder per asset: `assets/<category>/<asset_id>/` with `asset.json`, `source/` and `exports/`. Categories: `environments/kits`, `environments/locations`, `materials`, `characters`, `props`, `effects`, `audio`, `ui`.
- `source/` holds the only originals. `exports/` and `builds/` are disposable and ignored: never save a unique file there.
- Caches (Houdini geometry and simulation caches, Blender bakes) stay outside the repository.
- Record the exact Blender, Houdini and Unreal versions in `asset.json`. Do not guess a version.
- Do not rename Unreal modules, change the engine version, or move the Unreal project unless asked.
- Do not copy an asset that already lives in the Unreal project into `assets/`.
- Binary sources under `assets/` use Git LFS (see `.gitattributes`). Run `git lfs install` once before the first commit.
- Design decisions are the owner's. Mark your ideas as proposals.
